title: Sustained Multi-Priority Load and Stability Benchmark

method.edge_load: Two bounded CPU workers on Edge EC2, 60 seconds
method.metrics: Live Edge and Cloud metrics, no synthetic scheduler snapshots

observations: Edge CPU remained at 100% for all eight pressure-phase samples.
Cloud CPU remained low at the initial pressure snapshot while Cloud handled the majority of requests.
One High-priority request executed on Edge as best effort during the pressure phase.
At the start of the nominal recovery phase Edge CPU was still 100%; it reduced to 56.1% at round five and approximately 2% by round six.
The scheduler continued choosing Cloud during early recovery while Edge remained overloaded, then moved workloads back to Edge as Edge metrics recovered.
Five HTTP 503 responses had no inference result; the benchmark did not capture their response bodies, so the exact scheduler decision/reason is not asserted.
All 43 completed inference responses contained three detections.
limitations: Three concurrent requests per round; this is not a high-concurrency capacity ceiling test.
The 48-request test was performed in short rounds with a one-second inter-round pause, not a constant-rate open-loop generator.
The five HTTP 503 response bodies were not retained, so they cannot be conclusively attributed to queue decisions versus another orchestrator-level 503 condition.
The test uses a controlled CPU busy-loop to create Edge pressure.
Detection counts were captured, but no ground-truth model accuracy evaluation was performed.
Observed end-to-end latency includes scheduler metrics collection and orchestration overhead.
